newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Along with recent figures on the labour market, housing and non-dwelling construction, yesterday's release of merchandise imports data for December was another indication that the Australian economy is set to bounce back strongly from the slow-down of the past year. The continuing strength of the Australian sharemarket also supports strengthening growth, with the All Ordinaries Index finishing yesterday at an all-time closing high of 2444.2. Page 1.

Senior Macquarie Corporate Finance executive Simon Hannes has been charged with breaching section 31 of the Financial Transactions Report Act, following an investigation into unusual trading on September 18 and 19 last year by the Australian Securities Commission. Page 1.

The Australian Wheat Board announced yesterday that it had revised its estimate of the wheat harvest to 23 million tonnes and expected to pay growers an extra A$3 a tonne on most grades. AWB general manager merchandising, Ron Storey, said the pool return estimate has risen because of an "outstanding start" to the selling season. Page 5.

In a restructure of its booming Asian operations, National Mutual Life is planning to sell its Taiwanese business operations into the Hong Kong listed National Mutual Asia. This would leave National Mutual's Asian operations split between NM Asia and the Australian listed parent, National Mutual Holdings. Page 13.

FAI Insurances Ltd shares jumped to a 10-month high yesterday as it announced a partnership with American real estate guru Donald Trump. Under the deal, Trump will develop and market the Moritz Hotel in New York as condominiums and FAI wil be guaranteed the first US$180 million of any sales revenue. Page 13.

Canadian gold group Placer Dome Inc has extended its offer of 75 cents a share for Highlands Gold Ltd until next Saturday and Placer adviser, Macquarie Corporate Finance's Tony Ferguson, says there is no chance of Highlands providing a further restructurig proposal and a A$160 million underwriting agreement. Page 16.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following a three-month investigation by the Australian Securities Commission, Macquarie Bank Ltd senior executive Simon Hannes was arrested by the Australian Federal Police on Friday. Hannes has been charged with one count under the Financial Transaction Reports Act, which relates to conducting transactions to avoid reporting requirements. Page 19.

In a wide-ranging address at Westpac Bank's general meeting in Sydney yesterday, managing director Bob Joss highlighted the benefits of bank takeovers, saying "the economies of in-market mergers are powerful". Joss also warned Westpac could increase bankfees in the near future because of shrinking margins. Page 19.

Based on strong results from its Bluebird North and Cudingwarra deposits at Meekatharra, St Barbara Mines Ltd has upgraded its gold resource at its West Australian tenements to more than three million ounces. St Barbara chairman Alan Birchmore said Bluebrd North "appears a pretty robust mine", but further deep drilling is required to ascertain the extent of mineralisation. Page 20.

In response to a query from the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday, Casinos Austria International Ltd signalled a possible writedown of its investment in the embattled Reef Casino Trust Ltd. Company secretary Allan Tan said all decisions hinged on negotations between Reef and its financiers. Page 21.

In the group's December monthly production report, BHP attributed a 21 per cent decline in steel exports to shipment timings, but admitted that price and supply pressures persisted into the third quarter. However, steel production was stable, with domestc steel dispatches rising 12 per cent for the month. Page 21.

According to the latest Australian Bureau of Statistics figures, A$207 million was spent on oil exploration during the three months to September last year. Onshore activity rose more than 44 per cent to A$61.2 million, while offshore exploration was up b more than 12 per cent to A$145.8 million. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Speaking after yesterday's annual general meeting, Westpac Banking Corp managing director Robert Joss called for a further cut to interest rates to lift the sluggish economy. Joss said Westpac was on target to meet first quarter expectations, but higher fees and rigorous cost management would be needed to drive earnings growth. Page 25.

Charged in connection with cash transactions that occurred prior to unusual options trading in TNT last October, the arrest of Macquarie Bank executive Simon Hannes came as a complete surprise to the financial community. The brains behind the A$27 billion marriage of mining giants RTZ and CRA, Hannes was well respected by colleagues and seen as a quiet and conservative man. Page 25.

Following days of intense negotiations with their Japanese customers, Australia's iron ore producers, RTZ-CRA's Hammersley iron division and BHP Minerals, hope to achieve at least rollover prices. A spokesman for BHP and RTZ-CRA said the companies are cotinuing to argue for price increases to provide the capital return needed to invest in developing new sources of iron ore. Page 27.

A former employee of Fay Richwhite Futures Australia, Susan Bahr, appeared in St James Local Court yesterday on six charges of aiding and abetting a former colleague in unauthorised foreign exchange trading. The charges related to A$3.87 million trading over several months four years ago. Page 27.

FAI Insurances is set to enter an agreement with Donald Trump to turn New York's Moritz Hotel into apartments, in a deal that would see FAI receive the first US$180 million from the sale of the apartments and a share of profit thereafter. FAI chief execuive Rodney Adler said Trump would not receive any money from the deal until FAI had locked in its US$180 million. Page 27.

Despite a 65 per cent drop in December half net profit, St Barbara Mines lifted in the second quarter after reducing cash costs and pushing more ore through its Bluebird treatment plant near Meekatharra. Production at Bluebird rose 10 per cent on the preious quarter to 35,966 ounces. Page 29.
THE AGE

Senior Macquarie Bank corporate adviser Simon Hannes was arrested and charged on Friday in connection with unusual trading in TNT call options in late September. Macquarie Bank managing director Allan Moss said he believed Hannes would plead not guilty to the charge. Page C1.

Westpac managing director Bob Joss told shareholders at the bank's annual meeting yesterday that mergers among Australia's big four banks were very powerful strategies. Joss used Westpac's A$690 million takeover of Perth-based Challenge Bank in late 1995as an example of the efficiencies that could be achieved. Page C1.

With total remuneration over his five-year contract likely to top A$30 million, Westpac managing director Bob Joss defended his lucrative package yesterday, saying considering the difficulty of the job he undertook in 1993, the deal was fair. Westpac had just reported a A$1.56 billion loss when Joss started. Page C1.

In a bid to prepare for a major growth phase, Woodside Petroleum is planning to split its North-West Shelf operations from what it calls its northern operations. The move is also intended to eliminate any concerns Woodside's Shelf partners may have that t could spend their money on projects in which they are not involved. Page C1.

The Australian Securities Commission has referred the takeover conduct of superphosphate cooperative Pivot to the Corporations and Securities Panel, labelling Pivot's conduct as "unacceptable" after the cooperative terminated a A$450 million contract with Tasmanian company Gibson's just months before making a takeover offer for the company. Page C1.

With profits already hit by sharply lower prices worldwide and by weak domestic demand, BHP Steel's profits have taken another battering following an accident at its Port Kembla steelworks last Friday. The molten iron leak from the number five blast furnce means more than A$40 million in lost iron production for BHP. Page C1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
